newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson's missing Heisman Trophy turns up.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson's missing Heisman Trophy turns up.

text.p: The mystery surrounding O.J. Simpson's missing Heisman Trophy was partially resolved Wednesday after a lawyer for the family of Nicole Brown Simpson turned the trophy over to authorities.

The trophy, which could bring about $400,000 at auction according to a lawyer for the family of victim Ronald Goldman, was turned over to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Dept. by attorney Ira Friedman, who represents Nicole Brown Simpson's estate, a Sheriff's spokesman said.
But the spokesman said it was not clear where the trophy had been since February, when a civil court jury found Simpson liable for the murders.
Simpson was awarded the Heisman, by far the most valuable piece of property he currently owns, in 1968 as the best college football player in the United States.
He was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of Nicole Brown Simpson, his former wife, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, by a criminal court jury in October, 1995.

But in February this year a civil court jury found him liable for their deaths and ordered him to pay $33.5 million in damages to Goldman's father, Fred Goldman, his natural mother, Sharon Rufo, and Nicole Brown Simpson's estate, the sole beneficiaries of which are the two children by their marriage, Sydney and Justin.

The whereabouts of the trophy have been a mystery since Sheriff's deputies, acting on warrants issued on behalf of the plaintiffs, raided his mansion in the exclusive Brentwood section of Los Angeles and seized more than 100 household items, but could not find the Heisman.
Simpson has maintained he has no idea what happened to the trophy.

Municipal Judge Irving Shimer ordered Monday that several of Simpson's possessions, including table and floor lamps valued at over $6,000, as well as his golf equipment, could be auctioned to help satisfy the multi-million judgment against him. His mansion, valued at about $3.5 million, is in foreclosure as he has been unable to maintain his mortgage payments.
